entries.title: Kernel
entries.description: The core of macOS itself. It also uses CPU on purpose to keep the machine cool, so high usage here often means heat is being managed rather than something being wrong. Quitting it is not possible and would not help.

entries.title: Window Server
entries.description: Draws everything you see and passes your clicks to apps. It rises with the number of displays, high refresh rates and animation, so external monitors make it busier. Essential.

entries.title: launchd
entries.description: The first process macOS starts, with process ID 1. It launches and supervises every other service. Essential, and never quit it.

entries.title: Login Window
entries.description: Owns your login session and coordinates logging out and shutting down. Quitting it logs you out immediately.

entries.title: Dock
entries.description: The Dock, Mission Control and Stage Manager. Quitting it is harmless; macOS restarts it within a second.

entries.title: Finder
entries.description: The file manager and desktop. Safe to quit, and it comes straight back.

entries.title: Menu Bar Extras
entries.description: Draws the older style of menu bar item on the right of the menu bar. Quitting it restarts it and the icons reappear.

entries.title: Control Centre
entries.description: Control Centre and most of the modern menu bar items. Restarts on its own if quit.

entries.title: Stage Manager
entries.description: Handles Stage Manager and window tiling. Idle unless you use those.

entries.title: RunningBoard
entries.description: Decides which processes get to run, and suspends apps that are not in use. Part of how macOS keeps background apps cheap.

entries.title: Spotlight (index server)
entries.description: The Spotlight index server. It coordinates indexing but does little work itself; the heavy lifting happens in mds_stores and mdworker.

entries.title: Spotlight (indexing)
entries.description: Writes the Spotlight index. Heavy use is normal for a while after a large file copy, a migration or a macOS update, and it settles by itself. If it never settles, the index can be rebuilt.

entries.title: Spotlight (file reader)
entries.description: Reads individual files so Spotlight can index their contents. Many short-lived copies of it are normal.

entries.title: Spotlight (file reader)
entries.description: Reads individual files for the Spotlight index. Short-lived and started in batches.

entries.title: Spotlight (app data)
entries.description: Indexes data that apps hand to Spotlight, such as mail and messages, rather than files on disk.

entries.title: iCloud Drive
entries.description: Syncs iCloud Drive. Busy while files are uploading or downloading, quiet otherwise. The odd name is historical.

entries.title: iCloud
entries.description: Talks to iCloud for apps that store data there. Activity follows whatever is syncing.

entries.title: File Providers
entries.description: Runs cloud storage integrations that appear in Finder, including iCloud Drive, Dropbox and OneDrive.

entries.title: Time Machine
entries.description: Runs Time Machine backups. High disk and CPU use during a backup is the job being done, and it stops when the backup finishes.

entries.title: Background Downloads
entries.description: Downloads and uploads on behalf of apps in the background, including App Store and system updates.

entries.title: Push Notifications
entries.description: Keeps the connection to Apple's push notification service. Almost always idle.

entries.title: Photos (analysis)
entries.description: Scans your photo library for faces, scenes and duplicates. It runs hard for hours after a large import and then stops for good. It also waits for the Mac to be idle and on power.

entries.title: Photos (library)
entries.description: Manages the Photos library while Photos or anything reading from it is open.

entries.title: Media Analysis
entries.description: Analyses images and video for Visual Look Up and Live Text. Prefers to run while the Mac is idle.

entries.title: Core Audio
entries.description: Handles all audio input and output. Constant low usage while anything is playing is normal, and it never stops entirely.

entries.title: Audio Plug-in Scanner
entries.description: Scans audio plug-ins so apps can list them. Runs briefly after installing plug-ins.

entries.title: Wi-Fi
entries.description: Manages the Wi-Fi connection, including scanning for networks. Brief activity when networks change is expected.

entries.title: Bluetooth
entries.description: Manages Bluetooth devices and their connections.

entries.title: Sharing
entries.description: Powers AirDrop, Handoff, Universal Clipboard and screen sharing.

entries.title: Continuity
entries.description: Finds nearby Apple devices for Handoff, Sidecar and Continuity Camera.

entries.title: Bonjour
entries.description: Resolves names on your local network and finds printers, speakers and other devices. It is also involved in ordinary name lookups.

entries.title: System Configuration
entries.description: Tracks network configuration and tells apps when it changes.

entries.title: Network Quality
entries.description: Watches network conditions so the system can react to a poor connection.

entries.title: Application Firewall
entries.description: The macOS application firewall. Idle unless it is enabled and filtering.

entries.title: Certificate Checks
entries.description: Checks certificates when apps make secure connections. Frequent short bursts are normal; it is doing this on behalf of whatever is using the network.

entries.title: Keychain
entries.description: Manages keychains and cryptographic operations.

entries.title: Gatekeeper
entries.description: Checks apps before they run and enforces Gatekeeper. It is busiest the first time you open a newly downloaded app.

entries.title: Code Signing
entries.description: Verifies code signatures when programs start.

entries.title: XProtect
entries.description: Apple's built-in malware scanner. Runs occasionally and briefly.

entries.title: XProtect Scan
entries.description: Apple's malware remediation scan. Runs on a schedule, uses CPU for a few minutes, then stops.

entries.title: Directory Services
entries.description: Handles user accounts, groups and authentication.

entries.title: Privacy Permissions
entries.description: Enforces the privacy permissions you grant, such as camera, microphone and screen recording access.

entries.title: Preferences
entries.description: Reads and writes app preferences. Present for every user session and normally idle.

entries.title: Notifications (internal)
entries.description: Passes internal notifications between processes. Not the notifications you see on screen.

entries.title: Notifications (internal)
entries.description: Delivers low level system notifications between processes.

entries.title: Unified Logging
entries.description: Collects the system log. Brief activity is normal; sustained heavy use usually means something else is logging excessively.

entries.title: Diagnostics
entries.description: Collects diagnostic information when an app or the system asks for it.

entries.title: Power Management
entries.description: Manages sleep, wake and power assertions. It is what decides whether your Mac may sleep.

entries.title: Thermal Management
entries.description: Watches temperature and asks the system to slow down when needed.

entries.title: Launch Services
entries.description: Keeps track of which app opens which file type.

entries.title: Launch Services
entries.description: Registers installed apps and the documents they can open.

entries.title: Apple Events
entries.description: Routes automation messages between apps, including AppleScript and Shortcuts.

entries.title: System Events
entries.description: Runs small system plug-ins that react to events such as devices being connected.

entries.title: File System Events
entries.description: Records file system changes so apps can be told what changed. Busy while large numbers of files are being written.

entries.title: Document Versions
entries.description: Stores document version history for apps that support Revert To.

entries.title: Hang Reporter
entries.description: Samples an app that has stopped responding, so a report can be produced. Its presence means something else is stuck.

entries.title: Crash Reporter
entries.description: Writes a crash report after an app quits unexpectedly. Short lived.

entries.title: Swift Compiler
entries.description: Compiles Swift code. Heavy CPU use during a build is the build.

entries.title: Clang Compiler
entries.description: Compiles C, C++ and Objective-C code.

entries.title: Xcode (code intelligence)
entries.description: Provides completion and syntax checking inside Xcode. Can be heavy in large projects.

entries.title: Xcode (build system)
entries.description: Coordinates Xcode builds.

entries.title: Code Signing Helper
entries.description: Signs code during a build.

entries.title: Node.js
entries.description: A Node.js program. What it is doing depends entirely on which project started it.

entries.title: Terminal
entries.description: The Terminal app. Its CPU use usually belongs to whatever is running inside it.

entries.title: Web page (WebKit)
entries.description: One web page, in the process macOS isolates it in. Safari uses these, but so do Mail, Notes, the App Store and any app showing web content, so this does not tell you which app it belongs to.

entries.title: Web networking (WebKit)
entries.description: Fetches the network traffic for web content, on behalf of whichever apps are showing it.

entries.title: Web graphics (WebKit)
entries.description: Draws web content using the graphics chip, shared by every app showing a web view.

entries.title: Safari
entries.description: Safari itself. Individual pages run in separate processes, so a busy tab appears under Safari (web page) rather than here.

entries.title: Microsoft Defender
entries.description: Microsoft Defender's scanning engine. Sustained high usage on a developer machine usually means it is scanning build output; excluding build directories is the normal fix and is an IT decision on managed Macs.

entries.title: Microsoft Defender (managed)
entries.description: The managed component of Microsoft Defender, configured by your organisation rather than by you.

entries.title: Microsoft Defender (scanner)
entries.description: The part of Microsoft Defender that inspects files without elevated privileges.

entries.title: Microsoft AutoUpdate
entries.description: Checks for and installs updates to Microsoft applications.

entries.title: Browser tab or window
entries.description: One page or window of an app built on Chromium or Electron, which includes many desktop apps as well as browsers. Each tab gets its own process, so a heavy page shows up here rather than under the app itself.

entries.title: App graphics helper
entries.description: Draws the interface of a Chromium or Electron app using the GPU.

entries.title: App plug-in helper
entries.description: Runs a plug-in for a Chromium or Electron app, isolated from the app itself.

entries.title: App helper process
entries.description: A background process belonging to the app named before it. Chromium and Electron apps split their work across several of these.

entries.title: Firefox (page or plug-in)
entries.description: Renders one page or runs one plug-in for Firefox. Several are normal, and a heavy tab appears here rather than under Firefox.

entries.title: Firefox
entries.description: Firefox itself. Individual pages run as plugin-container, so a busy tab shows up there.

entries.title: Display Brightness
entries.description: Manages display brightness, Night Shift and True Tone.

entries.title: Nearby Devices
entries.description: Detects nearby Apple devices for AirDrop, Handoff and Continuity.

entries.title: Wi-Fi Direct
entries.description: Handles the direct device-to-device Wi-Fi used by AirDrop and AirPlay.

entries.title: Sidecar
entries.description: Runs Sidecar, which uses an iPad as a second display.

entries.title: Continuity Camera
entries.description: Lets your iPhone act as a camera or microphone for this Mac.

entries.title: Camera Service
entries.description: Registers camera devices so apps can use them.

entries.title: Wi-Fi Driver
entries.description: The Wi-Fi hardware driver, running outside the kernel as macOS now requires.

entries.title: Defender (network extension)
entries.description: Microsoft Defender's network filter, installed as a system extension by your organisation.

entries.title: Defender (endpoint security)
entries.description: Microsoft Defender's endpoint security extension, which inspects process and file activity as it happens.

entries.title: Performance Monitor
entries.description: This app. It samples what you see here, and pauses that sampling when no window is open. If it ever tops this list for long, that is a bug worth reporting.

entries.title: Location Services
entries.description: Works out where your Mac is, using Wi-Fi networks rather than GPS. Runs when an app or the system asks, including for time zone and weather.

entries.title: Find My
entries.description: Powers Find My, including the anonymous relay that helps locate other people's lost devices.

entries.title: Media Controls
entries.description: Handles play, pause and skip from keyboards, headphones and Control Centre.

entries.title: Video Decoder
entries.description: Decodes video on behalf of an app, in a separate process for safety. Active while anything is playing video.

entries.title: Siri Suggestions
entries.description: Stores the on-device usage patterns behind Siri Suggestions and Spotlight ranking.

entries.title: Shell
entries.description: A command line shell. Its CPU use belongs to whatever command is running inside it.

entries.title: Shell
entries.description: A command line shell. Its CPU use belongs to whatever command is running inside it.

entries.title: Spotlight (search window)
entries.description: The Spotlight search window itself, not the indexer. Indexing appears as mds_stores.

entries.title: Music
entries.description: The Music app.

entries.title: Mail
entries.description: The Mail app. Fetching and indexing a large mailbox keeps it busy for a while after setup.

entries.title: Spotlight (indexing)
entries.description: The group of background processes that build the Spotlight search index. They work hardest after a macOS update or when a lot of files change, and settle down on their own once the index is up to date.

entries.title: WebKit (web pages)
entries.description: The processes macOS uses to display web pages. Safari uses them, but so do Mail, Notes, the App Store and any app showing web content, so they cannot be traced back to a single app.

entries.title: Xcode
entries.description: Apple's development environment, together with the helpers it runs for building and for code completion. Heavy CPU use while a build or an index pass is running is expected.

entries.title: Claude (desktop app)
entries.description: Anthropic's Claude desktop application. Like other Electron apps it runs a helper process per window and per background task, which is why it appears as a group.

entries.title: Claude Code (command line)
entries.description: Anthropic's coding assistant running in a terminal. A different program from the Claude desktop app, which is why the two appear as separate rows.

entries.title: Microsoft Teams
entries.description: Microsoft's chat and meeting app. It runs a web view per window and a separate process for calls, so it usually appears as a group of several.

entries.title: Microsoft Teams (window)
entries.description: One Teams window or panel. Teams runs one of these per open view, which is why several appear at once.

entries.title: Microsoft Teams (add-ins)
entries.description: Runs the parts of Teams that load separately, such as meeting add-ins.

entries.title: WhatsApp
entries.description: The WhatsApp desktop app. Memory use grows with the number of chats and media kept open.

entries.title: OneDrive
entries.description: Microsoft's file sync. Busy while uploading or downloading, and quiet once everything is in step.

entries.title: Location Services
entries.description: Works out where the Mac is, for apps that ask and for things like time zone and Find My.

entries.title: Siri
entries.description: The background services behind Siri and the suggestions macOS makes. They run on device and wake briefly rather than working continuously.

entries.title: Siri (shortcuts)
entries.description: Handles Shortcuts and the actions apps offer to Siri.

entries.title: Siri (on-device knowledge)
entries.description: Keeps the on-device information Siri and Spotlight use to make suggestions.

entries.title: Suggestions
entries.description: Learns which apps you use when, so macOS can suggest them. Runs on device and is idle most of the time.

entries.title: Widgets
entries.description: Keeps widgets on the desktop and in Notification Center up to date.

entries.title: Notification Center
entries.description: Shows notifications and the panel they collect in.

entries.title: Spell checking
entries.description: Checks spelling and grammar for every app that uses the system text fields.

entries.title: Shortcuts (background)
entries.description: Runs shortcuts that are triggered automatically rather than by you opening the app.

entries.title: Microsoft Intune
entries.description: Applies the settings and policies an employer manages this Mac with. Present on work machines.

entries.title: Logi Options+
entries.description: Logitech's software for its mice and keyboards, handling button assignments and gestures.

entries.title: Logi Options+ (plug-ins)
entries.description: The part of Logi Options+ that adds per-app behaviour for supported applications.

entries.title: Virtual machine
entries.description: A virtual machine running through Apple's Virtualization framework, used by tools that run another operating system. Its usage is whatever is running inside it.

entries.title: Safari (platform support)
entries.description: Background helpers Safari uses for features such as extensions and web app support.

entries.title: Wallpaper (aerials)
entries.description: Plays the moving aerial wallpapers and screen savers. Only busy while one is on screen.

entries.title: Bitwarden
entries.description: A password manager. Like other Electron apps it runs several processes, and holds your vault decrypted in memory while unlocked.

entries.title: Metal shader compiler
entries.description: Compiles graphics code for apps and games as they need it. Busy in bursts when something starts or loads a new scene, then gone.

entries.title: Notifications (delivery)
entries.description: Delivers notifications and keeps the banners and badges in step with what apps have sent.

entries.title: Software Update
entries.description: Checks for and downloads macOS updates in the background. Heavy only while an update is downloading.

entries.title: App Store (background)
entries.description: Checks for app updates and handles purchases without the App Store window being open.

entries.title: Account sync
entries.description: Syncs Mail, Contacts and Calendar with the accounts you have added. Busy after a long time offline or when an account is first set up.

entries.title: Suggestions (on device)
entries.description: Works out what macOS should suggest next, from how you use the Mac. Runs on device and is idle most of the time.

entries.title: Quick Look
entries.description: Draws the preview you get when you press Space on a file. Appears while a preview is open and goes away after.

entries.title: App extension host
entries.description: Runs an extension an app provides, such as a share option or a widget, in its own process.

entries.title: AirDrop
entries.description: Finds nearby devices and transfers files to them. Active while the share sheet is open or a transfer is running.

entries.title: Apple Intelligence
entries.description: Runs the on-device part of Apple's writing and summarising features. Busy while one of them is working, idle otherwise.

entries.title: On-device model
entries.description: Runs a machine learning model locally, for features that work without sending anything to a server.

entries.title: Spotlight (managed data)
entries.description: Indexes app content that an employer's device management allows to be searched.

entries.title: Music library
entries.description: Keeps the Music and TV libraries in order and in sync. Busy after importing or a large library change.

entries.title: Weather
entries.description: Fetches forecasts for the Weather app, its widget and the menu bar.

entries.title: Weather (menu bar)
entries.description: The weather item in the menu bar.

entries.title: Weather (widget)
entries.description: The weather widget on the desktop or in Notification Center.

entries.title: Safari (fraud warning)
entries.description: Checks pages against Apple's list of known fraudulent sites, without sending Apple the page you are on.

entries.title: Notes (background)
entries.description: Handles Notes syncing and its share extension when the app itself is closed.

entries.title: OneDrive (sync)
entries.description: The part of OneDrive that does the actual uploading and downloading.

entries.title: Microsoft Teams (notifications)
entries.description: Shows Teams notifications, including while the main window is closed.

entries.title: Citrix Workspace
entries.description: Connects to applications and desktops hosted by an employer. Uses more CPU while a remote session is on screen.

entries.title: FortiClient
entries.description: The menu bar part of Fortinet's VPN and security client, usually installed by an employer.

entries.title: DisplayLink
entries.description: Drives extra monitors connected through a dock rather than a video port. Uses real CPU because it compresses the screen image itself.

entries.title: Performance Monitor (beta)
entries.description: The test version of this app, running alongside or instead of the released one.

entries.title: Charging chime
entries.description: Plays the sound and shows the flash when you plug in power. Runs for a moment and stops.

entries.title: Firefox (graphics)
entries.description: Draws Firefox's pages using the graphics chip. Named differently enough from firefox that only the glossary can connect the two.

entries.title: Logi Options+ (plug-in host)
entries.description: Runs one of the per-app plug-ins Logi Options+ provides.

entries.title: Logi Options+ (device link)
entries.description: Talks to the connected Logitech mouse or keyboard.

entries.title: Microsoft Defender (reporting)
entries.description: Sends Defender's health and detection reports to whoever manages this Mac.

entries.title: Network sign-in (802.1X)
entries.description: Signs the Mac in to a network that asks for credentials, as company and university Wi-Fi usually do.

entries.title: Spotify
entries.description: The Spotify music player. Like other Electron apps it runs several helper processes for its interface and playback.

entries.title: Microsoft Outlook
entries.description: Microsoft's mail and calendar app. Memory grows with the number of mailboxes and the size of the local cache.

entries.title: Adobe Acrobat
entries.description: Adobe's PDF reader and editor, together with the helper processes it runs for rendering and for its built-in browser.

entries.title: Adobe Acrobat (web view)
entries.description: The embedded browser Acrobat uses for its sign-in, document cloud and in-app pages.

entries.title: Adobe Acrobat (sync)
entries.description: Keeps Acrobat's fonts, settings and cloud documents in step in the background.

entries.title: Adobe Acrobat (updater)
entries.description: Checks for and installs Acrobat updates.

entries.title: Microsoft AutoUpdate
entries.description: Keeps Office, Teams, Edge and Defender up to date. Busy only while checking or downloading.

entries.title: Microsoft AutoUpdate (assistant)
entries.description: The background part of Microsoft AutoUpdate that watches for new versions.

entries.title: Windows App
entries.description: Microsoft's remote desktop client, formerly Remote Desktop. Uses more CPU while a session is on screen.

entries.title: Remote Desktop Manager
entries.description: Devolutions' tool for managing remote connections and credentials.

entries.title: Royal TSX
entries.description: A manager for remote desktop, SSH and VNC connections.

entries.title: Messages
entries.description: Apple's Messages app. Busy while syncing a long conversation history or loading attachments.

entries.title: boringNotch
entries.description: A third-party app that turns the notch area into a media and controls strip.

entries.title: DockDoor
entries.description: A third-party app that shows window previews when you hover the Dock.

entries.title: Logi Options+ (updater)
entries.description: Checks for updates to Logitech's mouse and keyboard software.

entries.title: System information
entries.description: The command macOS uses to gather hardware and software details. Apps run it briefly to read things like Bluetooth battery levels, and it disappears again.

entries.title: File copy
entries.description: The command macOS uses to copy folders while preserving permissions and metadata. Installers and backup tools run it; it exits when the copy is done.

entries.title: Rosetta
entries.description: Translates Intel apps so they run on Apple Silicon. Present only when such an app is open, and busy the first time each one starts.

entries.title: Continuity
entries.description: Keeps this Mac working together with your iPhone and iPad: Handoff, universal clipboard, phone calls and messages.

entries.title: Continuity (diagnostics)
entries.description: Records how well the Continuity features are working, on the device itself.

entries.title: App icons
entries.description: Draws and caches the icons apps use in the Dock, Finder and menus.

entries.title: Recent items
entries.description: Keeps the lists of recent documents, favourites and login items that the Dock and Finder show.

entries.title: Apple Account
entries.description: Handles signing in to your Apple Account and the keys that keep it secure.

entries.title: Touch ID and password prompts
entries.description: Shows the dialogs that ask for Touch ID, your password or your Apple Watch.

entries.title: Siri (learning)
entries.description: Learns from what you type and open so Spotlight and Siri can suggest things. Stays on the device.

entries.title: App sandbox setup
entries.description: Prepares the sandbox each app runs inside. Appears briefly whenever an app launches.

entries.title: In-app purchases
entries.description: Handles purchases and subscriptions made inside apps.

entries.title: Battery and performance logging
entries.description: Records battery health and performance figures for Apple's diagnostics and the Battery settings.

entries.title: System sounds
entries.description: Plays alert sounds and interface effects.

entries.title: Contact pictures
entries.description: Prepares the photos and Memoji shown for contacts in Messages, Mail and Contacts.

entries.title: Extension registry
entries.description: Keeps track of the extensions apps provide, such as share options, widgets and Finder actions.

entries.title: Wallet
entries.description: Manages the cards and passes in Wallet, and Apple Pay.

entries.title: Apple Pay fraud checks
entries.description: Checks payment requests against Apple's fraud protections.

entries.title: Mail (background)
entries.description: Fetches and indexes mail while the Mail app itself is closed.

entries.title: Bluetooth (your session)
entries.description: The part of Bluetooth that belongs to the logged-in user, handling pairing prompts and device access.

entries.title: Video encoding
entries.description: Compresses video for screen recording, screen sharing, FaceTime and video export. Heavy use is expected while any of those are running.

entries.title: Malware scanning
entries.description: Part of XProtect, the malware checking built into macOS. Runs when something new is opened or downloaded.

entries.title: iCloud sync
entries.description: Copies changes between this Mac and your other devices through iCloud.

entries.title: Share sheet
entries.description: The panel that appears when you share something. Exists only while it is open.

entries.title: Text previews
entries.description: Draws the little previews of text documents shown in Finder and Quick Look.

entries.title: App update download (Sparkle)
entries.description: Downloads an update for an app that uses the Sparkle update framework. Several apps share this name, so it does not say which one.

entries.title: Accessibility permission prompt
entries.description: The dialog asking whether an app may control your Mac through Accessibility. Appears only when something requests it.

entries.title: Managed app installs
entries.description: Installs and updates the apps an employer's device management pushes to this Mac.

entries.title: Migration Assistant
entries.description: Copies accounts, apps and files from another Mac or a backup. Only present during a migration, and heavy while it runs.

entries.title: Personal Voice
entries.description: Builds the synthetic voice recorded in the Personal Voice accessibility feature. Runs only while the Mac is idle and plugged in.

entries.title: Apple diagnostics upload
entries.description: Sends the diagnostic reports you agreed to share with Apple, if you did. Nothing is sent when sharing is off.

entries.title: Accessory firmware updates
entries.description: Updates the firmware of connected accessories such as AirPods and Apple keyboards.

entries.title: USB network driver
entries.description: Drives a network adapter connected over USB, including tethering from an iPhone.

entries.title: App Store offers
entries.description: Handles the offers and subscription reminders the App Store shows.

entries.title: App Store offers (on device)
entries.description: Stores the App Store's offer data locally so choosing what to show needs no server.

entries.title: App Store ads privacy
entries.description: Keeps App Store ad measurement on the device, without identifying you to advertisers.

entries.title: Advertising privacy
entries.description: Manages the personalised-advertising setting and keeps the identifiers it uses local.

entries.title: Home (energy)
entries.description: Collects energy readings from HomeKit accessories for the Home app.

entries.title: Accessibility visuals
entries.description: Applies visual accessibility settings such as reduced motion, increased contrast and pointer size.

entries.title: Feature availability
entries.description: Works out which macOS features are available for your region, language and account.

entries.title: Siri (data handling)
entries.description: Manages what Siri keeps on the device and what it is allowed to send.

entries.title: iCloud Keychain recovery
entries.description: Holds the escrow that lets you recover your iCloud Keychain on a new device.

entries.title: Contacts suggestions
entries.description: Notices names and addresses in your mail and messages so Contacts can suggest them. Stays on the device.

entries.title: App and website links
entries.description: Checks which apps a website has authorised, for shared passwords and links that open in an app.

entries.title: Music (cloud library)
entries.description: Keeps your Music library in step with iCloud and Apple Music.

entries.title: Spotlight (web results)
entries.description: Fetches the web suggestions Spotlight and Safari's search field show. Only active while you are typing a search.

entries.title: App suggestions
entries.description: Works out which app or shortcut to suggest next, from how you use the Mac.

entries.title: Certificate transparency
entries.description: Checks that the certificates websites present have been publicly logged, which is how forged ones are caught.

entries.title: Find My
entries.description: Keeps this Mac findable and helps locate your other devices and AirTags.

entries.title: Screen Time (usage)
entries.description: Records how long apps and websites are used, for the Screen Time reports.

entries.title: Screen Time
entries.description: Applies the Screen Time limits and downtime you have set, and syncs them across your devices.

entries.title: Messages (Siri)
entries.description: Lets Siri read and send messages on your behalf.

entries.title: Messages (storage)
entries.description: Keeps the message database on disk, including attachments and search.

entries.title: FaceTime and Messages (storage)
entries.description: Stores call history and message data shared between FaceTime and Messages.

entries.title: Managed app installs (your session)
entries.description: The user-side half of managed app installation, which shows progress and prompts.

entries.title: Lock screen posters
entries.description: Prepares and syncs the lock screen and contact poster images.

entries.title: Login items (your session)
entries.description: Shows the notice when an app adds itself to your login or background items.

entries.title: Login and background items
entries.description: Keeps the list of apps allowed to start at login or run in the background, as shown in System Settings.

entries.title: Game Mode
entries.description: Decides when Game Mode turns on, which gives a game priority on the CPU and GPU.

entries.title: Touch ID prompts (your session)
entries.description: The user-side half of the Touch ID and password dialogs.

entries.title: Dock (helper)
entries.description: Handles part of the Dock's work, such as drag and drop and window previews.

entries.title: Spotlight (Notes)
entries.description: Indexes the contents of Notes so they can be found in Spotlight.
